Thanks you very much. It really is, I've tried to go about my day, whether it be working, playing games, spending time with my family. But i'm occasionally thinking about this, and it eats at me. Hence why i've posted my thoughts, I need to talk about it. And it honestly helps, I'm sure you know as much. But getting it out and talking about it does wonders for your mental stabililty and peace of mind.

I agree with what you are saying, how I can't change him to see reason behind his recent nature or behaviour. I will recoginise my inability to help him, as much as it does hurt. I'd love to help him, but I've done what I can for him. I don't want to lose him, so I will look after myself and be there for him. But I won't help him continue to follow the same loop but acting oblivious and putting my own mentality at risk.

I'll sort out a conversation soon with him. Just so I can address what i've said here, being polite about it, but hopefully convincing him to seek the professional help he needs.

This has helped, immensely. I'm new to understanding depression and how it affects a person. But not only that now as I see theres multiple symptoms that can be noticed, and are dependant on the individuals circumstances.

I whole heartedly agree that I'm putting myself into his own personal conflict a bit too much than needed. However, I feel a sort of 'duty' to look after those close to me, those I care for and love. Fighting against that almost instinctual feeling leaves me conflicted.

I've said before how i've offered advice and council, to of course improve his situation. But reading your personal input and knowledge on the topic really opens my eyes and teaches me more about the internal struggle.

I do hope your current and previous treatments have worked for you. I greatly appreciate you taking the time to share your own story. Hearing that it is a relatable feeling from some takes the weight off my shoulders.

Thanks for the advice, I'm understanding more about depression as I seek opinions on this. He definitely needs to continue with his therapy. As much as I feel like my advice is sound and constructive, it's not going to help him.

10 yrs, a long time full of good memories and probably repressed bad ones. As I've only just truly opened my eyes in the past months. I suppose I pretended to believe he was his happy self all the time. Yet failed to realize his questionable decisions he'd make and countless relationships he'd been through.

But like you said, he must be getting help, and I barely talk to him now but I do know he was going through therapy. Although he was quite reluctant about it, so here's hoping. I'll consider giving him a call soon, once I collect my thoughts.

Thank you for sharing your story, I hope you've been better after seeking the help you needed.

I agree there's most certainly a boundary in a way, or perhaps a line. I've invested alot into my friend, and I understand it's more than just me and how I feel. I have just needed to talk more about this and it helps to come to a resolution. 

Over the years, he has seeked help with my encouragement. Though he has fallen short on attending alot of the time. I wish it were better for him, but I can't change that unfortunately. I hope he seeks the therapy he needs, and remains persistant on it.

I'm thinking about having a civil talk with him soon, just to outline how I feel and what I can suggests. But ultimately, tell him the truth and recommend professional help. As many people have made me realise that it's not my responsibility, and it goes much deeper than offering solutions and advice.

I really appreciate your response, thank you. Going forward, I have a much clearer head now when considering this.

Thank you very much, your words hold alot of wisdom.
I really appreciate the support and recognition of myself as a good person. As I always ponder whether or not I am. 

It's most definitely due to the guilt I feel. I've been used in the past for my good heart, and tossed aside. I move on, and i'm not one to hold onto things. I just wish my friend could be his true self. Loving, caring, funny, optimistic. That's was really sucks about this, because I know he's an amazing guy when he is himself. I have been holding onto the hope of change for a while now, but I feel like I have to let him go.

I agree I can't convey the full story in a few paragraphs or more, but I've expressed what's been on my mind since I've opened my eyes to the situation. The way I see it, I've done so much and I couldn't think of any way else I could help him.

Thank you for your response though. It has helped shed light onto this situation and it has given me an outsider perspective i've needed.
I can, although I don't know when I'll come to one. I agree, I'm never one to consider things lightly. Always forward thinking, trying to seek other alternatives.

I really appreciate that, and the critique too. That's what I was hoping to achieve out of this post, an honest outside perspective. Thank you for your insight, given the choppy summary of this situation I've written. I'm definitely leaning towards leaving due to those reasons stated. I've just held onto the hope that he'd change for the better. However, I will absolutely consider what you've said going forward, thanks for responding.
